newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO STOCKS END SUBDUED TRADE MODERATELY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO STOCKS END SUBDUED TRADE MODERATELY HIGHER.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished a subdued session moderately higher on Thursday, supported by a rally in shares of semiconductor equipment makers and bargain hunting in other blue-chip issues, brokers said.
The market was also relieved by Mitsui Construction Co Ltd's restructuring plan announced on Wednesday, giving a boost to the contractor's shares, but many other builders lost ground, they said.
The Nikkei 225 average climbed 214.02 points or 1.13 percent to close at 19,222.62. September Nikkei futures rose 250 points to 19,280.
Among chip equipment makers, Tokyo Electron Ltd rallied 330 yen to end at 7,650 yen, after briefly surging to a record high of 7,750.
Advantest Corp was up 700 yen at 12,500. It briefly touched a high for 1997 of 12,700 yen.
Other high-tech firms that make chip equipment also jumped in active trade. Nikon Corp ended 190 yen higher at 2,510, after briefly hitting a record high of 2,520. Canon Inc was up 180 yen at 3,730.
On Wednedsay, Applied Materials' shares surged after it reported earnings far exceeding Wall Street's expectations.
By sector, gainers were led by precision instruments, trading houses, electric equipment, automobiles and sea transport. The major losers were brokerages and electric power.
The second section index gained 9.76 points to end at 1,669.28, with 6.05 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 7.0 points at 1,072.24, posting a gain for the first time after falling on Wednesday for the 33rd straight session.
